entries.finding: ketone line says ketones come from oxidising 'an alkanol', unscoped
entries.reason: Only a secondary alkanol oxidises to a ketone; primary gives an aldehyde then an acid, tertiary resists. The unscoped wording teaches a false general rule.
entries.change: C line now reads 'made by oxidising a secondary alkanol'.

entries.finding: hint 3 lets the student answer without thinking

The proposed fix rests on familiarity ('a sugar you have already met') and an unsupported claim that mannose appears nowhere else in the syllabus, which is weaker teaching.

entries.finding: hints 2 and 3 together rule out catalyst, concentration and pressure, leaving temperature by elimination

entries.finding: exam tip says magnesium 'reacts only with steam'
entries.reason: Magnesium reacts slowly with cold water to give the hydroxide, which the syllabus also teaches; 'only' is an unscoped absolute.
entries.change: Exam tip now reads 'A metal that reacts well only with steam'.
